latest_final: Kameda was a monarch, while Umio was a non-royal political leader who opposed the faction aligned with Kameda. Umio was assassinated by someone acting for an opposing faction, and his body was deliberately denied proper burial—a dishonoring treatment that suggested he had been defeated. Kameda’s body, by contrast, was cremated as customary practice, not as a sign of victory. Comparing the contrasting treatment of their remains, observers inferred that Umio had probably lost the political struggle.
